each node keeps its own ObservedReviewRequest record (id prefixed with its own node id) and the store-level task query in CreateOneAsync sees the peer\\u0027s task only when replication lands, about two minutes later, after both dispatchers have claimed; the record names the two aggravating facts from the incident (the loser\\u0027s twin queued under a per-project ceiling of 0 on one node and was claimed on the other after replication, and the two nodes ran different auto pr-review modes because the setting is node-scoped)\u0022,\u0022Convergence on replication: when a pr-review task arrives by replication (task_added header originNodeId set) whose external reference already has a live pr-review task in this store, the younger of the two (by UUIDv7 id, deterministic on every node with no coordination) is abandoned as a duplicate before any dispatcher can claim it, with an abandon reason naming the survivor; a replicated younger duplicate arriving after the local one is already claimed is abandoned and its run retired; the mirror case where the local task is the younger one abandons the local task; the existing already-covered fast path test still passes\u0022,\u0022h9k status and the courier feed show the abandoned duplicate once, as a duplicate of the survivor, never as a needs-you row\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022Evidence, from both nodes (2026-09-24). Two facts that shaped the incident: the Mac\\u0027s arx-platform per-project ceiling was 0, so the Mac-born twin queued there and was claimed on Windows after replication (every duplicate run was a Windows run); and the two nodes ran different modes (Mac normal by default, Windows first explicit), because ProjectSettingsChanged is EventScope.NodeScoped and never replicates. mt_doc_observedreviewrequest ids are prefixed with the observing node id by design (Decisions Log #161), so no node reads another\\u0027s record; do not try to share them. The hold-before-mint layer (wait one replication interval before a first mint) is a separate task stacked on this one; do not implement it here. Aggravators: the Mac\\u0027s arx-platform per-project ceiling was 0, so the Mac-born twin queued there and was claimed on Windows after replication; and the two nodes ran different modes because ProjectSettingsChanged is EventScope.NodeScoped. Since 2026-09-24 20:23 EDT the Mac has arx-platform auto pr-review off, so the live race is closed for that project by configuration; this fix is for any project two nodes both watch. Design, settled by the challenge session of 2026-09-24 20:41 EDT (verdict in this task\\u0027s journal.md): the decision is NOT made in the replication inbox (EventReplicationInbox is a bare replay with no side effects, commits per record, and a later replicated TaskClaimed from the origin node would flip an abandoned twin back to Claimed because TaskAggregate.Apply(TaskClaimed) sets state unconditionally). It is a standing convergence pass in AutoPrReviewEngine, a sibling of ConcludeWithdrawnAsync (near line 1033), run every sweep and also called from MessageSweepEngine right after a replication read that applied events (near line 329) so the abandon lands within seconds; plus a claim-time refusal in DispatchEngine.TryClaimAsync (near line 1526) beside the placement and tracker gates, which is the actual guarantee. The daemon abandons as the owner (node.OwnerId, ConcludeOneAsync\\u0027s precedent near line 1179). TaskAbandoned is ProjectScoped and replicates; Apply(TaskAbandoned) is idempotent; TaskDecider.Abandon refuses a terminal task, so the pass reads state first. Owner scope through TaskDecider.IsGrantedToThisOwner (fingerprint when present, else owner id; DispatchEngine near line 1696) and WasAutoPrReviewCreated (TaskListItem near line 170). Run retirement: no new termination code; GenerationFence.AllowsAsync(refuseAbandonedTask: true) at every pr-review dispatch site (PrReviewEngine near lines 561, 926, 1061; RunSupervisor exit handler near 1470) already retires a run whose task is Abandoned at its next phase boundary (test at PrReviewTaskEngineTests near line 1872). SweepExpiredLeasesAsync skips tasks not Claimed (DispatchEngine near line 270), so the pass must delete this node\\u0027s TaskLease and append ReleaseHolder for an Abandoned task it holds (TaskAbandonCommand lines 47 to 52 are the shape). Mention carry-over through TaskDecider.ObservePrReviewMention. UUIDv7 is DomainId.New (UUIDNext, Postgres-friendly); compare ids in one place (bytewise ORDER BY and Guid.CompareTo agree). Criterion 3 already holds today (TaskListItemProjection is inline; the fast path near line 455 and the existing query near line 704 filter on reference and state only) and needs only a test seeded by replication. Test harness: EventReplicationTests (OpenStoreB, SeedQueuedTaskAsync, EventReplicationOutbox.QueuePendingAsync, MessageOutbox.FlushAsync, EventReplicationInbox.ReadFromAsync over InMemoryMessageTransport and FakeLedger; A_replicated_claim_never_dispatches_locally_and_shows_HeldElsewhere near line 1612) plus PrReviewTaskEngineTests.ScriptedGh (near line 390) for the engine. Rendering: ReviewRequestPane.Covering picks live-first, TaskStatusComposer groups Abandoned as Archived, the courier feed renders TaskAbandoned as \\u0027abandoned: \\u003Creason\\u003E\\u0027, so criterion 6 costs the reason wording and tests. The hold layer is task 1cccd3f7, blocked by this one; stay out of DecideAsync, RecordObservationAsync, ObservedReviewRequest, and DaemonOptions so the two do not collide. Design, settled by the challenge session of 2026-09-24 20:42 EDT (verdict in this task\\u0027s journal.md): a symmetric hold is a no-op on the collision because both nodes pay it and the gap between their mints never changes (the three incidents had sightings 7 to 32 s apart against 83 to 119 s of replication). The rule is asymmetric: the node whose id sorts lowest among the owner\\u0027s currently enrolled, unrevoked nodes mints on the first sweep, every other node holds. The hold is measured off GitHub\\u0027s own RequestedAt (read fresh every tick near AutoPrReviewEngine line 483, already a mint precondition), not ObservedReviewRequest.FirstObservedAt, so a node waking late mints at once and nothing new is persisted. The hold sits after the four questions DecideAsync already asks (covered, time known, past cutoff, setting on; near lines 393 to 507) and before CreateOneAsync, so the gh pr view import is never paid while held; speed (First, Now, Normal) is decided inside CreateOneAsync and stays blind to the hold. The enrolled set is TrustedOwner.Nodes from ILedgerChainReader.ComputeAsync, a git fetch the message sweep already does per project every 15 to 45 s (MessageSweepEngine near line 133) and never persists; the engine must not fetch: a small in-process holder the message sweep writes its last chain per project into, read by the engine; no chain yet, a chain naming only this node, or no ledger at all all read as leader (today\\u0027s behaviour). EventOriginProgress (peers seen so far) is the wrong source: it lingers for a revoked node. Setting shape follows MessageActivePollMinSeconds (DaemonOptions near line 132, whole seconds, not TimeSpan): a nullable on OperatingSettings with a Default const, a key in PlatformConfigFile (near lines 317 and 340), an option on ConfigSetCommand (near line 232), a ConfigShowCommand row with origin (near lines 94 to 99), the daemon-status line; #584\\u0027s effort knob is the freshest walk of that path. Default 300 s (the 3-minute poll interval plus a replication allowance); zero means this node never defers. Status: one new ReviewRequestOutcome (HeldForPeer), one entry in FromInput (ReviewRequestOutcome.cs near line 78, so an older CLI does not render it Unknown), one Compose branch in ReviewRequestPane ahead of the closing informational one (near lines 370 to 373); IsReportable fires on outcome change so the two log lines fall out of the existing Info line near engine line 588; Settle\\u0027s hiccup clause keeps HeldForPeer through a tick that cannot read the time. Decision logic is a pure function in AutoPrReviewObservation (my node id, enrolled node ids, RequestedAt, now, hold) so most tests need no Docker; the engine reads DateTimeOffset.UtcNow directly (near lines 551, 760, 1149), control age through the scripted timeline\\u0027s requestedAt. Two-store harness: EventReplicationTests (OpenStoreB, FakeLedger, InMemoryMessageTransport, outbox flush then inbox read, near lines 62 to 130) with PrReviewTaskEngineTests\\u0027 scripted gh and PollOnceAsync. Mentions are out of scope: DecideMentionAsync mints through CreateFromMentionAsync and the mention record is a one-shot dedupe; the convergence layer already settles a mention twin; a follow-up may apply the leader rule there. Known hazard, accepted: a newly enrolled node with a lower id is invisible to the old leader until its next chain compute (15 to 45 s), so for one sweep both may mint; convergence settles it.
